prompt:
Take the first reference photograph and change ONE thing in it: the markings
painted on the road.

Everything else stays exactly as it is: the same Berlin street corner from
the same camera position, the same vertical framing, the same deserted
pavement, the same pedestrian traffic light on its grey pole with the upper
round lens glowing an even plain red, the same pale cream facade with its
stone-framed windows, the same black city bicycles along the wall, the same
granite kerb, the same flat overcast daylight.

THE ONE CHANGE is the markings painted at the bottom of the picture: the
pedestrian crossing stands under the traffic light, and the red bicycle
strip holds ONE EVEN WIDTH along its whole length and TURNS.

The pedestrian crossing begins at the granite kerb directly below the grey
pole that carries the traffic light, on the RIGHT of the picture, and runs
from there toward the bottom edge: broad white bars painted on the grey
asphalt, the same bars as in the second reference photograph. Beyond them,
on their right, the road is plain grey asphalt to the right edge of the
picture.

The red bicycle strip lies to the LEFT of the crossing. Coming up from the
bottom edge of the picture it runs straight toward the kerb, as wide as a
bicycle lane; at the kerb it bends to the LEFT and follows the street,
running along beside the kerb and leaving the picture at its left edge,
still exactly as wide there as at the bend. It is one continuous ribbon of
red asphalt with a dashed white line along each of its two edges, and one
white bicycle pictogram painted flat on it below the bend.
